description: Taunton is the county town of Somerset and a lovely place to explore on foot. There's an anicent castle, three picturesque public parks, two canals, riverside footpaths, several local woodland areas, nature reserves and lots of great walking options in the nearby Blackdown Hills AONB. This circular waterside walk takes you along the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal to the neighbouring village of Creech St Michael before returning along the River Tone. The easy walk runs for a distance of just under 7 miles, passing Bathpool and some interesting old bridges on the way. You can extend the walk by heading west from the town along the Grand Western Canal. This runs from Taunton to Tiverton in Devon. Also in the town is the waymarked Taunton Heritage Trail which visits several of the town's historic properties. For more detail on the Landmarks, Nature Reserves and History of the town please see the informative wikipedia page.

details.subtitle: Pubs/Cafes
details.content: The Ring of Bells is a good choice for some post walk refreshments. They serve good quality food and have a large sunny garden for summer days. You can find them at 16-17 St James Street with postcode TA1 1JS for your sat navs.

details.subtitle: Dog Walking
details.content: The canal and river paths make for a fine dog walk. The Ring of Bells mentioned above is also dog friendly.

details.subtitle: Further Information and Other Local Ideas
details.content: Just to the south of the town there's something of a hidden gem at the Trull Waterfall. The picturesque spot is located just east of Trull village and has a viewing bridge and nice trails along the Sherford Brook. Just to the north is the historic Hestercombe House where you can explore the beautiful gardens of the old country house. The Somerset Space Walk runs along the towpath of the Bridgwater canal. The route is lined with a number of interesting sculptures representing the planets of the Solar System. You can see the scale model of the sun at Maunsel Lock and the description panels next to the sculptures to find out more. For more walking ideas in the area see the Somerset Walks page.
